codeAB.summary: Lyonet's contemporary clear decipherment, imaged on the DECODE record and transcribed here.
codeAB.en:
I cannot refrain from informing you of a muffled rumour that has spread here, of a supposed prophecy made by a man
living in Amsterdam, who, while telling Mr Thomas Hop that the ship he was worried about had not been taken by the
English but had perished at such-and-such a latitude, added that he also knew that an attempt was to be made on His
Majesty's life on the 15th of this month. I shall know by tomorrow whether these words were really spoken, and in that
case I shall not lose an instant in asking that this madman be shut up in the madhouse.

R2067.summary: D'Affry sends "B" a copy of what M. ...tier wrote to him (the loan extract read in R1074).
R2067.en:
I have the honour to send you today a ciphered copy of what Mr Astier wrote to me. It seemed to me useless to attempt
any money operation in England itself, which, if it came to be discovered, would make our needs appear greater than
they are and would cause the precautions to be increased. Despite these precautions the English will still invest with
us when the interest can tempt them, and they still have at present, with bankers of this country and at Brussels,
funds that could not find a place in our life annuities. I know that there are here two or three young Englishmen, one
of whom is called Macdonald. If he is really leaving France, and it is of interest to know where he is going and what
he is doing, I shall try to put myself in a position to give you an account of it. Two Spaniards have arrived here
from Paris, one of whom is Mr de Lastiri, Secretary of the Embassy at Paris.
